blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — From transforming household waste into fertilizers and school chairs to turning discarded coconut husks and waterlilies into livelihood opportunities, the Villar Foundation has spent more than three decades promoting community-based solutions to environmental problems. Established in 1995 by former Senate President Manny Villar and former Sen. Cynthia Villar, the foundation’s environmental initiatives demonstrate how proper waste management can help protect waterways, support agriculture, create jobs, and improve community life. Among its flagship programs are the Sagip Ilog, or the Las Piñas–Zapote River Rehabilitation, and Riverdrive Projects, which combine river cleanup, waste management, and community participation.
